_doc: A PLANTING RECORD for the 1812 scene (T-2497): the Kinzie house's poplar row and the two cottonwoods behind it, read by renderers/web/js/trees.js through data/flora/index.json and scoped there to scene 1812, so they stand in no other year. Zone z10_settled_town is named because it is the record that describes both species as planted and grown trees; the Kinzie establishment is the one settled ground on the north bank in 1812.
name: The Kinzie house's four Lombardy poplars and two cottonwoods

existence.note: THE POPLARS: Currey (1912, ch. II) has John Kinzie plant 'four Lombardy poplars at the foot of the slope on which the house stood' after he bought the house in 1804; Wau-Bun describes them standing in 1831. Nothing dates the planting before August 1812, so their standing in this scene is inferred from a planting after 1804 and a row still standing in 1831, and from Lossing's view, which draws them against the first fort. THE COTTONWOODS: Wau-Bun, describing 1831, 'Two immense cottonwood-trees stood in the rear of the building'; trees immense in 1831 stood in 1812.

The household Sarony plate and1857 engraving draw the row advancing from the piazza toward the river, not stretching east along the bank as the old planting did. This north/south row stays in the newly bounded green's eastern part, E1156.0, at4.0m stations from N331.2 to319.2. Exact coordinates/orientation/spacing are reconstructed from the house and committed bank, not surveyed from image pixels. L-kinzie-house-completion-2484. ONE OF THE TWO COTTONWOODS BEHIND THE HOUSE. Wau-Bun, of 1831: 'Two immense cottonwood-trees stood in the rear of the building, one of which still remains as an ancient landmark'; data/exclusions.json kinzie_house adds that they are 'separately attested and one survived into the 20th century'. Every picture draws a great broad crown behind the house. Where each stood is this record's own: behind the house, toward either end. Moved 3.5 m north at T-2485 (from N +349.0), when the bake-house the pictures draw behind the house's west end took the ground just behind it; the renderer keeps a stem 4.5 m clear of every footprint. HEIGHT 21 m, inside the species' 18-26 m band in z10_settled_town: trees 'immense' in 1831 were already grown in 1812.

research_note: WHAT WOULD MOVE THESE. A measured plan of the Kinzie lot or a planting account locating the trees rather than naming them. Sarony's lithograph after Juliette Kinzie's household sketch is now in the public image store as chicago_kinzie_residence_sarony_currey_1912.png and source sarony_kinzie_residence_currey_1912_plate; it was directly read with all six other pictures for T-2484. The four north/south poplar stations, exact spacing and all six heights/positions remain reconstructed in L-kinzie-house-completion-2484, not surveyed from image pixels. The four stations are N331.2,327.2,323.2,319.2 at E1156,4.0m apart: the north stem clears the actual house footprint by4.80m against the renderer's existing4.5m margin. T-3106's in_structure names only the green's fenced plot; it never exempts the house, other buildings or travelled tracks. Both cottonwoods keep their existing coordinates, species and heights. The ByGrade colours describe their inferred species appearance; these exact planting positions and heights remain liberties.
